newsitem.title: USA: Pemex sells first Mayan crude to L.A. in six years.
newsitem.headline: Pemex sells first Mayan crude to L.A. in six years.

text.p: State-owned Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) sold a cargo of Mayan crude oil to a Los Angeles refinery Friday, the first sale of the grade into southern California in six years, market sources said Monday.
The cargo of viscous, high sulphur crude is sized at 360,000 barrels to be delivered in August, sources said.

Mexico's state oil monopoly Pemex has been looking for new markets for its crude, especially its additional supply of heavy Maya. An aggressive production program has left Pemex with an increased amount of Maya to sell.
Negotiations have been complicated by strict emissions regulations in Los Angeles which prohibited the refining of Maya, which has an API content of 22 and contains toxic hydrogen sulphide.

Earlier, traders said the price formula for West Coast shipments of Maya would be an average of West Texas Intermediate (WTI), Alaska North Slope (ANS), and California's heavy Kern River crude prices, minus an unspecified discount.
The sale follows months of speculation that Pemex would sell spot Mayan crude into southern California once the region's refiners conducted trial runs.
